audit.why: Darius owns levels 1-5 and the side lane; level 6 is the one even stage. The entry says this and the win rate near 50 supports it. Apprehend at 26s against Arctic Assault at 18s is the structural reason level 6 equalises rather than flips — she gains a 1300-range opener he has no dash to answer, but he still wins the fight if the pull is up when it lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text says that at 2+ items 'Darius's Hemorrhage and Noxian Guillotine are far less threatening when you have 250+ armor and magic resist'.
audit.why: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage and scales with Hemorrhage stacks on the target — resistances are irrelevant to it, and Apprehend's passive additionally makes Darius's physical damage ignore a percentage of armour, so the two abilities named are precisely the two that his opponent's armour does not answer. This is the same inversion the Cho'Gath entry makes about Feast: it tells a tank that tank items solve an execute that ignores tank items. The reader will hold ground at low health at exactly the wrong moment.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text now separates Hemorrhage, which items do answer, from Guillotine and the Apprehend armour-pen passive, which they do not.
sources: champ-data/_kits/darius.json (R Noxian Guillotine trueDamage, cd 120/100/80; E Apprehend passive armour penetration)

audit.whatIsWrong: Frost Armor's slow immunity against Crippling Strike is absent from all seventeen fields, Apprehend's cooldown is never given despite the entry calling it 'a long cooldown', Decimate's healing is never connected to anti-heal, and early names Decimate as Darius's W.
audit.why: Crippling Strike is how Darius keeps a target inside the Decimate blade, and Fury of the North grants immunity to slows outright — so a Sejuani with Frost Armor up cannot be held there, which changes the disengage from a hope into a rule. That is the single most useful thing to tell a Sejuani in this matchup and it appears nowhere. Apprehend at 26 seconds at rank 1 is the longest cooldown either champion has, and 'his pull is on a long cooldown' without the number gives the reader nothing to count. Decimate heals him off every champion the outer blade catches, which is why extended fights slip away, and the entry never tells the reader to buy Grievous Wounds. Finally, Decimate is his Q — calling it W in the first sentence of early misdirects a reader who is trying to learn his cast order.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor's slow immunity is now in whys[5], late and breakdown.cooldowns. Apprehend's 26s is in whys[3], wants.you[1], early and breakdown.cooldowns. Grievous Wounds and Decimate's heal are in late. Decimate is labelled (Q) in early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/darius.json (Q Decimate heal, cd 9/8/7/6/5; W Crippling Strike slow, cd 5; E Apprehend cd 26/23.5/21/18.5/16)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and late refer to 'your passive Permafrost resistances'.
audit.why: Permafrost is a 1.5s targeted stun and carries no resistances. They come from Frost Armor on Fury of the North, and only after Sejuani has been out of combat — which against a champion whose passive is a five-second bleed is a real constraint the phrase erases. Hemorrhage keeps her in combat, so Frost Armor stays off for the whole duration of his bleed, and that is worth knowing.
audit.corrected: whys[5] and late now name Frost Armor and describe it returning between trades.

edits.after: At level 1 Darius takes Decimate (Q) and immediately out-damages you — the outer-ring blade heals him off champions and Hemorrhage bleeds every melee who stands next to him, and you have no reliable answer at this stage. Take W, last-hit at range where you can, and do not trade. At level 2 Apprehend comes online: if he pulls you while you have only Q or W, you eat a full bleed stack with no escape and lose a third of your health bar for free. Your level 3 combo (Q-charge into double-W into Permafrost) is your first honest moment — bait his E on a fake step-up, and if it misses you have 26 seconds at rank 1 to work with, the longest window either of you gets. Q in, both W arcs to fill the Frost gauge, then stun. Without Apprehend he cannot stop you walking out after it, and the Hemorrhage he started never fully stacks. Save the combo for that exact moment — never burn Q into a Darius who still has his pull.
edits.before: At level 1 Darius takes W (Decimate) and immediately out-damages you — his empowered Q outer-ring heal and Hemorrhage bleed are designed to punish every melee who stands next to him, and you have no reliable answer at this stage. Take W, last-hit with ice-shard range where you can, and do not trade. At level 2 his Apprehend comes online: if he pulls you at level 2 while you have only Q or W available, you will eat a full bleed stack with no escape and lose a third of your health bar for free. Your level 3 combo (Q-charge into double-W into E stun) is your first honest moment — if you bait his E on a fake step-up and it misses, that is your window to Q in, W twice for Frost stacks, and E stun him. Without Apprehend he cannot stop you from walking out after the stun, and the Hemorrhage he started never fully stacks. Save that combo for that exact moment — do not burn Q into a Darius who still has his pull ready.

edits.after: Once you have Sunfire Aegis and a second tank item, Hemorrhage runs out of steam and Frost Armor comes back between every trade, which also makes you immune to the Crippling Strike slow he uses to hold you in the blade. Buy Grievous Wounds before any long fight: Decimate heals him off every champion the outer ring catches. You become the engagement tool your team needs — Arctic Assault into a backline carry, Glacial Prison on the second target, Winter's Wrath filling the gauge on the whole cluster for a chain stun. Darius becomes a frontliner you stun and ignore. The lane sits near 50-50 precisely because neither of you rolls the other: you survive the early, he loses the late.

notes:
The packet reports zero defects and five sequencing cues for this matchup, and it was still the entry with the second-largest factual problem in the slice. spikes[3].text told a tank that 250 armour answers Noxian Guillotine, which is true damage. Cho'Gath's entry makes the identical claim about Feast. Two matchups in one slice inverting the same rule suggests the generator does not know which abilities are flagged trueDamage, even though both kit files carry the flag.

'Decimate' was labelled as Darius's W in the opening sentence of early. It is his Q.
